dedupe_keys.name: world bank global payment systems survey gpss

description: The Global Payment Systems Survey is conducted by the World Bank among national and regional central banks and monetary authorities to gather information on the status of payment systems worldwide. It combines quantitative and qualitative measures covering every aspect of national payment systems: infrastructure, the legal and regulatory environment, technological and business model innovations, international remittances and oversight frameworks, plus payment system reforms and the factors that hinder or help them. Findings guide international and national policy dialogue and World Bank Group technical assistance. Coverage is global, by responding authority. Access to the survey page is free; the formats of results and the licence are not stated on the page read. Caveats: answers are self-reported by authorities, waves are several years apart, and not every country responds to every wave. For simulation it describes the structure, operators and oversight of national payment infrastructures, useful as reference data for financial infrastructure system descriptions and governance comparisons. Related catalogue records include the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics and the Global Findex Database.
